The divergence is real and worth tracking precisely because credit can flip: if SLOOS tightens or HY OAS widens, the same concentration turns rotation into unwind.

themes.counterRead: The screen's own behavior is the counter-read: if these were clean sentiment dislocations, the promotion engine would have promoted at least one. Zero promotions plus a live earnings-miss headline elsewhere in the same screened universe says the tag cannot separate a sentiment cut from a guidance break. Treat the pile-up as a verification queue — name by name — not a basket buy.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree on the squeeze, and the disagreement inside the data is the point: restrictive nominal rates with tight credit spreads and contained breakevens is a valuation headwind for small caps and long-duration equity, not a credit event. Cash-flow-today names keep the bid until either the 10-year breaks or spreads crack — the Oct 27-28 FOMC is the next dated hinge.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve prices restriction: DGS10 at 5.27%, DGS30 at 5.64%, real 10-year at 2.91%, 2s10s at +0.44, DFF at 3.88%.
